clue.text: See check applied to the Spanish material

indicators.note: one piece is put against another, so the check follows the Spanish article

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for Latin vide, see, used in references
el is the Spanish masculine word for 'the'
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect some fabric once a Spanish label is attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied to' sets VET against V plus EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvet is a soft fabric with a dense pile, an example of material.

clue.text: European driver is able to get going

parts.note: a motive is what drives someone to act

explanation.surface: A European motorist is fit to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist but means the force that drives a person; 'get going' is to stir the feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotive stirs people up, so it can get them going emotionally.

clue.text: Score one increased in French game

parts.note: a score is twenty, which in French is vingt
one with something added is 'and one', in French et un

explanation.surface: A tally rising by one during a match played in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French: twenty, then 'and one', making twenty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Vingt-et-un, twenty-one, is the card game also called pontoon or blackjack, named in French.

clue.text: Implied leaders in talks are cautious in tone

indicators.note: the leaders of the following words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Diplomatic suggestions hinted at by careful heads of negotiating teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like heads of delegations but asks for the first letters of five words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood without being stated, that is, implied rather than spoken.

clue.text: They rapidly pass border in record time

indicators.note: the border is placed within the record and time pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: Athletes overtaking at a boundary in a record-breaking run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They rapidly pass' sounds like runners but means short-lived things.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that last only briefly, which quickly go by and vanish.

clue.text: Ruler in mood beheaded other ranks

indicators.note: the head, its first letter, is cut from the word for mood

parts.note: a temper is a mood, as in 'in a good temper'
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A sovereign in a foul temper has the common soldiers executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the first letter of TEMPER, leaving EMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme sovereign of an empire.

clue.text: Barbarism appears to excite physicist

parts.note: to heat up is to excite or inflame
Joseph Henry was an American physicist; the henry, unit of inductance, is named after him

explanation.surface: Savage behaviour that seems to stir up a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenry is heathen practice, the uncivilised state once contrasted with Christian civilisation.

clue.text: Factotum looking up excellent thing

parts.note: a man, as in man Friday, is a servant who does everything

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters go upward, read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A household servant glances upward at something wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' turns AI into IA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Thing' can mean an obsession or craze, as in 'he has a thing about trains'.

clue.text: Sharp answer in Tripos test

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the two clue words

explanation.surface: A smart reply given during a Cambridge University examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the honours exam at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, cutting retort, a sharp reply.

clue.text: Ruin cocoa when replanted around phosphorus mine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the symbol
plants set out again in new places suggest the letters being rearranged

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: Spoiling a cocoa crop by replanting it near a phosphate mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a pit but is the definition: a rich source.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine can mean an abundant source, as a horn of plenty overflowing with good things is.

clue.text: Maybe hairline fracture's closing after sleep

indicators.note: the last letter follows the word for sleep

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A tiny crack in a bone finally knits while the patient sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairline fracture' reads as one phrase, but 'Maybe hairline' is the definition, the hairline being found at the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the neck is where the hairline often lies, so it may be called that loosely.

clue.text: Hoax about rubbish presented as decree

indicators.note: turned about, the word for hoax is read backwards

parts.note: to kid is to hoax or fool
tat is shoddy rubbish

explanation.surface: A prank about junk passed off as an official order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses KID to DIK.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh order imposed by authority, a decree.

clue.text: Participate in show trial?

parts.note: a show trial sounds like a rigged court case, but a trial of a show is a practice run before opening night

explanation.surface: Taking part in a political court case staged for propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: The political sense is the decoy; a trial run of a stage show is what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a play before performance is taking part in a trial of the show.

clue.text: Pick up extremely huge feet

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Lifting enormous feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To heft is to lift something, especially to judge its weight.

clue.text: Much water tears through low area

indicators.note: the tears run through the word for low, splitting it

parts.note: base means low or mean
rents are tears or rips

explanation.surface: A flood of crying sweeps across a low-lying region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like weeping, suiting 'water', but is rips, RENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barents Sea is part of the Arctic Ocean north of Norway and Russia, a large body of water.

clue.text: Seemingly beardless without a fine covering

indicators.note: 'without' in the old sense of outside: the phrase for beardless goes round the letter

parts.note: a bald chin appears to have no beard

explanation.surface: A man apparently clean-shaven, lacking a smart face covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldachin is an ornate canopy of rich fabric over a throne or altar, a fine covering.

clue.text: Ruined kids' home capturing hearts in Arab territory

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the card suit's letter inside them
a ruined thing is wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A wrecked children's home winning affection in an Arab land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' scrambles KIDSHOME, and 'capturing' takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikhdom is a state ruled by a sheikh, as found across the Arab world.

clue.text: Cedric Errol fortunately flustered only a single time

indicators.note: flustered means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up
the word holds the time abbreviation twice, and one must go so it appears just once

explanation.surface: A boy named Cedric Errol luckily got rattled only once.
explanation.walkthrough: FORTUNATELY has two Ts; 'only a single time' drops one (T = time), and 'flustered' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedric Errol is the boy hero of Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel Little Lord Fauntleroy, known by that title.

clue.text: Native American artist parking in two areas visits house

indicators.note: the artist and parking letters go inside the two area letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two of them give A and A
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A tribal painter parks in two zones before calling at a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Maintained high position — fell reportedly

indicators.note: as reported by word of mouth, so the word for fell is said aloud

parts.note: rain fell, it rained

explanation.surface: Someone held a lofty post and then, so they say, toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' seems to oppose 'high position', but means came down as rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigned held the throne, the highest position in the land.

clue.text: Notice in last places one puts up today

indicators.note: the last places of the words are their final letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A notice put up today among the bottom-ranked finishers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a posted sign but is the verb, to catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to spot or notice.

clue.text: Locks put on cable rising in gorge

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the word for gorge

parts.note: to pig is to gorge, eat greedily

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: wire is cable

explanation.surface: Padlocks fixed to a cable climbing up a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' is hair, not padlocks, and 'gorge' is a verb, not a ravine; 'rising' turns WIRE into ERIW.
explanation.definitionFit: A periwig is a wig, an artificial set of locks of hair.

clue.text: Princess and cool patriarch returned to dismiss bishop

indicators.note: dismissing means sending one letter away from the rest
sent back, the words for cool and patriarch are read in reverse

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
Abraham is the biblical patriarch
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A royal lady and a calm church elder come back to sack a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns INABRAHAM round to MAHARBANI; 'to dismiss' removes B.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharani is an Indian princess or queen, wife of a maharaja.

clue.text: Pest wants assistance outside pub

indicators.note: the word for assistance wraps round the pub

parts.note: aid is assistance
PH, public house, is a pub as marked on maps

explanation.surface: A nuisance outside the pub wants help.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid, such as a greenfly, is a sap-sucking insect pest of plants.

clue.text: Girl involves royal couple in charlatanism

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the royal pair into itself

parts.note: Fay is a girl's name
K for king and ER for queen (Elizabeth Regina) make a royal pair

explanation.surface: A young woman drags the king and queen into a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlatanism is the practice of a quack, which is fraud or sham pretence.

clue.text: Well-known American FBI agent detains

indicators.note: the agent holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent, as of the FBI

explanation.surface: A notorious US federal agent makes an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed means celebrated, widely known.

clue.text: What occurs in tub at home?

definitions.text: What occurs in tub at home?

indicators.note: asks for the letters found inside the run of the next three words

explanation.surface: A question about what happens in the tub at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a soak in the tub at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a wash taken lying in a tub, typically at home.

clue.text: Passed on my request for feathers

definitions.meaning: given on to a younger person after earlier use, like old clothes
asking someone to pass me the down, soft feathers

explanation.surface: Someone asks for some feathers that were inherited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feathers' reads as plumage; down is fine feathers, so the request is 'give me down'.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment worn first by an older sibling and given to a younger is passed on.

clue.text: Tricked about party — that's forgiven

indicators.note: the word for tricked goes about the party

parts.note: conned means tricked
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone was duped over a party, and all is pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Condoned means overlooked or pardoned, accepted without punishment.

clue.text: Woman honoured to cover silver cost

indicators.note: the honoured woman wraps round the symbol

parts.note: a dame is a woman given an honour, the female knighthood
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A decorated lady pays to plate something with silver.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, Dame is the title given to a woman honoured like a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What's the damage?' asks what something costs, so damage means cost, informally.
